messages:
maria: FYI the onboarding sample app hit a funky rerank bug. Batching 8 queries -> server returns mixed embedding lengths (384 vs 512) in same response. Only shows up when we trigger an auth refresh during the request.
devon: ugh. which SDK and sampleapp? node/python?
maria: Python sampleapp v0.9.1 using requests with urllib3 PoolManager. Repro steps: run sampleapp with short-lived token, send 8-item embed batch, expire token mid-flight, let SDK refresh and retry. Sometimes the response array contains one or two embeddings with smaller dims.
lee: do we have raw response? can you paste minimal snippets (no floats, just lengths)?
maria: raw excerpt:
```
{"data":[{"id":0,"embedding":[...384 floats...]},{"id":1,"embedding":[...512 floats...]},...],"model":"redwood-embed-1"}
```
devon: That screams stream interleaving or leftover bytes from previous request on same socket. urllib3's connection pooling can return a reused connection if previous response wasn't fully drained. If retry happens, new request may get leftover bytes parsed as part of response.
lee: Interesting — Node team saw something similar with keepAlive and axios. This would be an SDK-level flaw, not server. But we should harden server too. If runtime sees inconsistent embedding dims in same batch, it should return 5xx or at least include a validation error.
maria: Agreed. Short-term: add strict shape validation in the Python SDK client — if any embedding.len != expected, surface an SDK error and drop the batch. Also instrument a metric for "mixed_embedding_size".
devon: Agreed. Longer term: patch urllib3 usage: call response.close() or ensure .stream() drains before returning connection to pool. Also consider disabling pool reuse on auth-refresh retry path.
lee: I'll file an internal issue for server-side validation: runtime should check per-response items all have same dimension for the model and return an error code with diagnostic. We should also add a regression test to eval harness that simulates token expiry and ensures no interleaved payload.
ci-bot: created issue #8721 (runtime: validate embedding lengths per response)
devon: I'll open a Python SDK PR: python-sdk#512 — validate embedding shape + raise EmbeddingShapeError, emit metric to telemetry. Quick patch will be to validate len(e) == expected_dim for every embedding in response.
maria: For the sampleapp, I patched retry logic to call resp.close() and to use PoolManager.connection_from_url(..., block=True). That reduced occurrences in local e2e.
lee: Good. For docs: we need a short troubleshooting note in DevEx onboarding: "If you see inconsistent vector sizes during batching, upgrade SDK or disable connection reuse while retrying auth refresh." @doc-bot can you add?
doc-bot: added troubleshooting blurb to docs/devex/embeddings-troubleshooting.md (PR pending)
maria: One gotcha: different models have different dims (redwood-embed-1=512, redwood-embed-compact=384). Make sure SDK logs model name + expected dim when erroring so users can quickly see mismatch cause.
devon: Also add an SDK integration test that forces token expiry by returning 401 mid-stream and confirms that retry path either yields clean response or raises the shape error.
ci-bot: pipeline queued for python-sdk/shape-guard (#512) :gear: job 8201
lee: OK next steps: 1) runtime validation issue (#8721) 2) python SDK PR (#512) 3) sampleapp e2e update to simulate token expiry 4) docs blurb. Assign owners and we can close this thread after green CI.
maria: I'll run e2e and report back. Creating a tiny repro script also and sharing in #devex if people want to run locally.
maria: follow-up: ran 50 iterations forcing token expiry; before patch ~7 failures with mixed dims, after patch shape validation caught 7 and surfaced error; after adding resp.close() + disabled pool reuse on retry -> 0 mixed dims.
devon: great, ship when CI passes. we'll track runtime guard separately. Thanks! :clap:
